correctness.rationale: All twenty vertices and thirty edges of each graph are specified exactly. BFS and Floyd–Warshall independently agree on 20×20 distance matrices. All 1,140 unordered triples are tested; 540 and 720 forbidden. Full increasing-order face enumeration yields all simplices with face vectors (20,190,600,550,60) and (20,190,420,370,60), no dimension above four. Complete boundary-squared checks pass. Independent row-based and column-based exact bitwise Gaussian elimination agree on boundary ranks (19,161,379,60) and (19,131,289,60). Thus reduced mod-two Betti vectors are (0,10,60,111,0) and (0,40,0,21,0); both Euler characteristics are -60. The executable package was run successfully.

originality.rationale: No inspected source determines either complete mod-two Betti signature of the graph-geodesic vertex-subset complex for both twenty-vertex Petersen double covers. The closest same-graph topological comparison is an induced-matching complex with graph edges rather than vertices as simplex vertices, with distinct face restrictions; its homotopy theorem has no implication about the present chain complexes. The two foundational general-position papers establish the admissibility condition and counting notions, not these homology groups. An unindexed equivalent computation remains possible.

value.rationale: The dodecahedral and Desargues graphs are canonical nonisomorphic cubic twenty-vertex double covers of the Petersen graph and have equal Euler characteristics -60 and equal 60 top-dimensional simplices in their geodesic general-position complexes. Their exact differing ranks of first, second and third mod-two homology show that these coarse shared data and their common quotient fail to determine the topology. This is a natural, complete finite comparison of an invariant beyond graph cardinalities, not an arbitrary unmotivated numerical slice.
